title: Cavern Club
fact: Opened on 16 January 1957 as a jazz club, it regularly hosted the Beatles in their early years.

title: Royal Albert Hall
fact: Opened by Queen Victoria in 1871, it has hosted the BBC Proms every summer since 1941.

title: Sydney Opera House
fact: Designed by Danish architect Jørn Utzon, it was opened by Queen Elizabeth II on 20 October 1973.

title: Carnegie Hall
fact: Built by industrialist Andrew Carnegie, it stands at 881 Seventh Avenue in Midtown Manhattan.

title: Hollywood Bowl
fact: Its bandshell sits against the Hollywood Hills, with the Hollywood Sign to the northeast.

title: Red Rocks Amphitheatre
fact: Its seats are flanked by two huge sandstone monoliths, Ship Rock and Creation Rock.

title: Apollo Theater
fact: Home of the TV show Showtime at the Apollo, it stands on West 125th Street in Harlem.

title: Hitsville U.S.A.
name: Hitsville U.S.A. (Motown)
fact: Motown founder Berry Gordy bought the house in 1959 and made it the label's headquarters and studio.

title: Electric Lady Studios
fact: Jimi Hendrix commissioned it in 1968 but recorded there for only ten weeks before his death.

title: Capitol Records Building
fact: Completed in April 1956, the 13-story tower stands just north of Hollywood and Vine.

title: Whisky a Go Go
fact: On the Sunset Strip, it was central to the Los Angeles music scene from the 1960s to the 1990s.

title: CBGB
fact: The letters stood for Country, Bluegrass, Blues, yet the club became famous for punk and new wave.

title: Stax Museum of American Soul Music
name: Stax Records studio (Soulsville)
fact: The label's name joins its founders' surnames: Jim STewart and Estelle AXton.

title: Muscle Shoals Sound Studio
fact: Formed in 1969 by the Muscle Shoals Rhythm Section after they left nearby FAME Studios.

title: Hansa Studios
fact: It stands about 150 metres from the former Berlin Wall, hence the nickname 'Hansa by the Wall'.

title: Olympia (Paris)
name: L'Olympia
fact: Opened in 1893 by a co-creator of the Moulin Rouge, it is on the Boulevard des Capucines.

title: Wiener Musikverein
name: Musikverein
fact: Designed by Theophil Hansen, it has housed the Vienna Philharmonic since it opened in 1870.

title: Vienna State Opera
fact: Built from 1861 to 1869, it was the first major building on the Vienna Ring Road.

title: La Scala
fact: It opened on 3 August 1778 with Antonio Salieri's opera Europa riconosciuta.

title: Bayreuth Festspielhaus
fact: Richard Wagner built it himself, and it is dedicated solely to his stage works.

title: Elbphilharmonie
fact: The concert hall sits on top of an old brick warehouse, Kaispeicher A, in Hamburg's HafenCity.

title: Paradiso (Amsterdam)
name: Paradiso
fact: Built in 1880 as a church for a free congregation, it became a music venue in 1968.

title: Roskilde Festival
fact: Created in 1971 by two high school students and a promoter, it is the largest festival in the Nordic countries.

title: Wacken Open Air
fact: Held every August since 1990, it has been called the 'Mecca of heavy metal'.

title: Tomorrowland (festival)
name: Tomorrowland
fact: First held in 2005 in De Schorre park, it was conceived by brothers Manu and Michiel Beers.

title: Montreux Jazz Festival
fact: Held each July on the shore of Lake Geneva, it is the world's second-largest annual jazz festival.

title: Isle of Wight Festival
fact: So many people came in 1970 that Parliament restricted large overnight gatherings on the island.

title: Sziget Festival
fact: Held on Óbuda Island in the Danube, it grew from a low-profile student event in 1993.

title: Exit (festival)
name: Exit Festival
fact: It was traditionally staged inside the Petrovaradin Fortress in Novi Sad.

title: Bolshoi Theatre
fact: Its Bolshoi Ballet is by far the biggest ballet company in the world.

title: Teatro Colón
fact: The present theatre opened on 25 May 1908 and is renowned for its acoustics.

title: Nippon Budokan
fact: It was built for the first Olympic judo competition, at the 1964 Tokyo Games.

title: Massey Hall
fact: Opened in 1894, it was a gift to the people of Toronto from industrialist Hart Massey.

title: Preservation Hall
fact: This jazz venue on St Peter Street in the French Quarter gets about 180,000 visitors a year.

title: The Fillmore
fact: Built in 1912 as the Majestic Hall, it became the Fillmore Auditorium in 1954.

title: Ronnie Scott's Jazz Club
name: Ronnie Scott's
fact: This jazz club in Soho has been operating since 1959.

title: Palais Garnier
fact: It was built for the Paris Opera from 1861 to 1875 at the behest of Emperor Napoleon III.

title: Gewandhaus
fact: Home of the Leipzig Gewandhaus Orchestra, today's hall is the third to bear the name.

title: Rudolfinum
fact: Its Dvořák Hall is home to the Czech Philharmonic and a main venue of the Prague Spring festival.

title: Rockfield Studios
fact: This residential studio in the Wye Valley was founded in 1963 by brothers Kingsley and Charles Ward.

title: Compass Point Studios
fact: Island Records founder Chris Blackwell set it up in 1977, 16 km west of downtown Nassau.

title: New Afrika Shrine
fact: It replaced Fela Kuti's original Afrika Shrine, which burned down in 1977.

title: Fuji Rock Festival
fact: Named after its first event at the base of Mount Fuji in 1997, it moved to Naeba Ski Resort in 1999.

title: The Rolling Stones
fact: Their first stable line-up was Mick Jagger, Keith Richards, Brian Jones, Bill Wyman and Charlie Watts.

title: Queen (band)
name: Queen
fact: Formed in London in 1970; Brian May and Roger Taylor had played together before in the band Smile.

title: U2
fact: Formed in Dublin in 1976 by Bono, the Edge, Adam Clayton and Larry Mullen Jr.

title: AC/DC
fact: Formed in Sydney in 1973 by brothers Angus and Malcolm Young.

title: INXS
fact: Originally called the Farriss Brothers, their name is a play on 'in excess'.

title: Nirvana (band)
name: Nirvana
fact: Kurt Cobain and Krist Novoselic founded the band in Aberdeen, Washington, in 1987.

title: Pearl Jam
fact: Formed in Seattle in 1990, they were a key band of the early-1990s grunge movement.

title: Metallica
fact: James Hetfield and Lars Ulrich formed the band in Los Angeles in 1981.

title: The Beach Boys
fact: Formed in 1961 by brothers Brian, Dennis and Carl Wilson, cousin Mike Love and friend Al Jardine.

title: Kraftwerk
fact: Ralf Hütter and Florian Schneider formed the band in Düsseldorf in 1970; the name means 'power plant'.

title: Rammstein
fact: Formed in Berlin in 1994, the band's six-man line-up has never changed.

title: Daft Punk
fact: Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo formed the duo in Paris in 1993.

title: Radiohead
fact: Formed in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, in 1985; their debut single was 'Creep'.

title: Arctic Monkeys
fact: Formed in Sheffield in 2002, they were among the first bands to find fame through the internet.

title: The Smiths
fact: Formed in Manchester in 1982, with Morrissey and Johnny Marr writing the songs.

title: Black Sabbath
fact: Before taking their name in 1969 they were the Polka Tulk Blues Band, and then Earth.

title: Crowded House
fact: Neil Finn, Paul Hester and Nick Seymour formed the band in Melbourne in 1985.

title: BTS
fact: Their Korean name, Bangtan Sonyeondan, means 'Bulletproof Boy Scouts'.

title: Sigur Rós
fact: Singer Jónsi often uses 'Vonlenska', the band's term for wordless vocals.

title: The Cranberries
fact: Formed in Limerick in 1989, they were first called The Cranberry Saw Us.

title: Simple Minds
fact: Formed in Glasgow in 1977 around Jim Kerr and Charlie Burchill.

title: A-ha
name: a-ha
fact: Formed in Oslo in 1982; their debut album was Hunting High and Low.

title: Roxette
fact: Per Gessle already fronted Gyllene Tider before forming Roxette with Marie Fredriksson.

title: Scorpions (band)
name: Scorpions
fact: Guitarist Rudolf Schenker formed the band in Hanover in 1965.

title: The Doors
fact: Formed in Los Angeles in 1965, with Jim Morrison on vocals.

title: Grateful Dead
fact: Formed in Palo Alto in 1965; their devoted fans are known as 'Deadheads'.

title: Talking Heads
fact: David Byrne, Chris Frantz and Tina Weymouth met as students at the Rhode Island School of Design.

title: Gipsy Kings
fact: Founded in Arles in 1979, the group was originally called Los Reyes.

title: Ladysmith Black Mambazo
fact: They became known worldwide after singing on Paul Simon's 1986 album Graceland.

title: Soda Stereo
fact: Formed in Buenos Aires in 1982, they are the best-selling Argentine band of all time.

title: Midnight Oil
fact: Formed in Sydney in 1972, with Peter Garrett as lead singer.

title: Led Zeppelin
fact: Robert Plant, Jimmy Page, John Paul Jones and John Bonham formed the band in London in 1968.

title: Bob Marley
fact: A pioneer of reggae, he became a global symbol of Jamaican music and culture.

title: Frank Sinatra
fact: Born to Italian immigrants in Hoboken, he was nicknamed 'Ol' Blue Eyes'.

title: Louis Armstrong
fact: Nicknamed 'Satchmo', he won a Grammy in 1965 for 'Hello, Dolly!'.

title: Aretha Franklin
fact: Rolling Stone twice named the 'Queen of Soul' the greatest singer of all time.

title: Jimi Hendrix
fact: Born Johnny Allen Hendrix, he began playing guitar at 15.

title: Bob Dylan
fact: He was born Robert Allen Zimmerman in 1941.

title: Prince (musician)
name: Prince
fact: Born and raised in Minneapolis, he pioneered the 'Minneapolis sound'.

title: Michael Jackson
fact: The 'King of Pop' popularised dance moves such as the moonwalk.

title: Madonna
fact: Born Madonna Louise Ciccone, she is known as the 'Queen of Pop'.

title: Beyoncé
fact: She rose to fame in the late 1990s as lead singer of Destiny's Child.

title: Kylie Minogue
fact: She is the highest-selling Australian-born female artist of all time.

title: Björk
fact: Born and raised in Reykjavík, she began her music career at the age of 11.

title: Édith Piaf
fact: Born Édith Gassion, she was discovered in Paris in 1935 by nightclub owner Louis Leplée.

title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
fact: Born in Salzburg, he completed more than 800 works in his short life.

title: Ludwig van Beethoven
fact: Born in Bonn, he was baptised on 17 December 1770.

title: Frédéric Chopin
fact: Born in Żelazowa Wola, he grew up in Warsaw and left Poland at 20.

title: Johann Sebastian Bach
fact: His works include the Brandenburg Concertos and the Goldberg Variations.

title: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky
fact: He was the first Russian composer whose music made a lasting impression internationally.

title: Antonio Vivaldi
fact: A virtuoso violinist, he made the solo concerto a widely followed form.

title: Giuseppe Verdi
fact: Born near Busseto, he came to dominate Italian opera after Rossini, Bellini and Donizetti.

title: Fela Kuti
fact: He is regarded as the principal innovator of Afrobeat.

title: Youssou N'Dour
fact: He helped develop mbalax and was Senegal's Minister of Tourism from 2012 to 2013.

title: Shakira
fact: She is known as the 'Queen of Latin Music'.

title: Antônio Carlos Jobim
fact: Also known as Tom Jobim, he is considered one of the fathers of bossa nova.

title: Freddie Mercury
fact: Born Farrokh Bulsara in Zanzibar in 1946, he became the lead singer of Queen.

title: Elton John
fact: Born Reginald Kenneth Dwight, he has written songs with lyricist Bernie Taupin for decades.

title: Ed Sheeran
fact: Born in Halifax, West Yorkshire, he was raised in Framlingham, Suffolk.

title: Celine Dion
fact: Born into a large family in Charlemagne, Quebec, she is the best-selling Canadian recording artist.

title: Drake (musician)
name: Drake
fact: He first became known playing Jimmy Brooks in Degrassi: The Next Generation.

title: Rihanna
fact: Born Robyn Rihanna Fenty, she debuted with Music of the Sun in 2005.

title: Ravi Shankar
fact: A sitar virtuoso, he helped bring Indian classical music to audiences worldwide.

title: A. R. Rahman
fact: Born A. S. Dileep Kumar, he has won two Academy Awards.

title: Lata Mangeshkar
fact: She recorded songs in over thirty-six Indian languages.

title: Buddy Holly
fact: He was born Charles Hardin Holley in Lubbock, Texas, in 1936.

title: Willie Nelson
fact: He was a main figure of outlaw country, known for Red Headed Stranger (1975).

title: Ray Charles
fact: He pioneered soul music in the 1950s and was nicknamed 'The Genius'.

title: Slim Dusty
fact: Born David Gordon Kirkpatrick, he was known as Australia's King of Country Music.

title: Joni Mitchell
fact: Born Roberta Joan Anderson, she has won eleven Grammy Awards.

title: Leonard Cohen
fact: A poet and novelist as well as a songwriter, he is in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

title: Jacques Brel
fact: A master of the modern chanson, he influenced David Bowie and Scott Walker.

title: Luciano Pavarotti
fact: Nicknamed the 'King of the High Cs', he was one of the Three Tenors.

title: Andrea Bocelli
fact: He rose to fame in 1994 by winning the newcomers' section of the Sanremo Music Festival.

title: Nana Mouskouri
fact: She has released an estimated 450 albums in at least thirteen languages.

title: Taylor Swift
fact: She is the highest-grossing live music artist of all time.

title: Johnny Hallyday
fact: Born Jean-Philippe Smet, he is credited with bringing rock and roll to France.

title: Miriam Makeba
fact: Nicknamed 'Mama Africa', she campaigned against apartheid.

title: Cesária Évora
fact: Famous for singing morna barefoot, she won a Grammy Award in 2004.
